summary: Reproduced the unbounded stdlib default on the prepared implementation: with os.cpu_count() reporting 384, BaseGrammarBackend created 32 workers. Automatic grammar compilation concurrency is now capped at max(1, min(cpu_count // 2, 8)), with SGLANG_GRAMMAR_COMPILE_MAX_WORKERS as a positive operator override and 0 selecting automatic sizing. The installed xgrammar API independently reports max_threads=8 by default, so limiting outer concurrency reduces the documented multiplier without changing xgrammar behavior.

tests.what_was_measured: Baseline suite passed 33 tests and 17 subtests; a separate runtime probe recorded os.cpu_count()=384 and executor_max_workers=32. See raw/baseline_unit.txt and raw/before_environment.txt.
The added regression failed before the implementation because the worker-sizing contract did not exist. See raw/regression_before.txt.

39 tests and 22 subtests passed, covering the 384-CPU cap, low CPU boundaries, missing cpu_count, positive override, zero-as-auto, and actual executor construction. A runtime probe recorded executor_max_workers=8. See raw/regression_after.txt and raw/after_executor.txt.
Formatting tool availability only: the prepared interpreter has no ruff module. No packages were replaced or installed.

gpu_evidence: The assigned single AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 was inventoried in raw/before_environment.txt, but this CPU thread-pool sizing change has no GPU numerical path. No model or serving workload was claimed.
remaining_limitations: The cgroup v1 CPU controller reports cpu.cfs_quota_us=-1 (no CFS quota), so production CFS throttling and decode TPOT degradation were not reproduced.
The change bounds outer compile concurrency but does not make CPU detection CFS-quota-aware.
xgrammar's default of 8 internal threads per compiler and duplicate submissions for identical in-flight uncached grammars remain unchanged.
No model weights were needed or used; no HTTP serving, semantic accuracy, full-model, or distributed-workload claim is made.
Ruff was unavailable in the prepared interpreter.
